sources.capture_method: Railway describe-environment, environment-status, service metrics, deployment list and build logs
Grafana Cloud datasource list, alert rule read, notification routing and contact-point read

latest_attempt.reason: Dockerfile cache mount ID lacks the required cacheKey prefix at line 26.

records.assessment: The currently active production deployment is successful, but the latest deployment attempt failed. These states are not contradictory: the previous successful deployment remains live while the newer main commit failed to build.

Memory usage is consistently close to 1 GB in the observed sample. The Railway service-config read did not expose a memory limit, so no percentage-of-limit or saturation threshold is asserted. The service requires capacity review and time-correlated telemetry.

PR #839 is the candidate fix for the measured Dockerfile/Railway cache ID issue. Its integration, OpenRewrite, CodeQL, container and canonical-plan checks passed in the capture; CI itself remained queued. No deployment recovery is claimed until the fix merges and a new production deployment succeeds.

Grafana returned 17 datasource records. The contact-point list was empty and the root notification receiver was 'empty'. The alert-rule read returned null rather than a structured rule list, and Prometheus query calls could not resolve the datasource UID despite it appearing in the datasource inventory. Live rule inventory and metric-to-alert delivery remain unproven.

anomalies: The latest production deployment attempt is FAILED while the previous deployment remains active SUCCESS.
No pending Railway staged changes were present.
Grafana's datasource inventory and Prometheus query adapter disagreed about datasource UID availability.
Alert rules could not be conclusively enumerated; do not treat a null read result as a verified zero-rule count.
assessment: W7 has partial operational truth, not operational maturity. Production currently serves from the 2026-11-15 successful deployment, the 2026-11-20 main deployment attempt fails Dockerfile validation, memory samples are high in absolute GB, and Grafana's notification receiver is empty. Required next proofs are a reviewed Railway recovery merge and successful deployment, memory limit confirmation, datasource query recovery, explicit alert-rule inventory, contact-point provisioning, end-to-end notification test, SLO consumption, and documented rollback/recovery exercise.
